title: Uttar Pradesh: Ayodhya, Prayagraj, Mathura–Vrindavan, Lucknow and Kushinagar
selection: Uttar Pradesh ranks first among Indian states for domestic tourism but VacayOut covered only Agra and Varanasi. This pack adds its other major pilgrimage and heritage cities, their main sights, two Agra/Varanasi additions, and state-wide itineraries and guides — researched from district administration sites, Incredible India, the Ram Mandir trust and Wikipedia.

AY1.claim: Ayodhya, on the banks of the Sarayu river, is revered as the birthplace of Lord Rama and is a major pilgrimage city.

evidence.quote: In the heart of Uttar Pradesh, along the banks of the sacred Sarayu River, lies the ancient city of Ayodhya. Revered by millions as the birthplace of Lord Rama

AY2.claim: Ayodhya was the capital of the ancient Kosala kingdom.

evidence.quote: It served as the capital of the ancient Kosala Kingdom.

AY3.claim: Ayodhya's art and culture show the influence of Vaishnavism, Shaivism and Jain and Buddhist faiths, and Nawabi rule left its mark on architecture and food.

evidence.quote: The art and culture of Ayodhya clearly reflect the influence of Vaishnavism, Shaivism, Shakya, Saurism, and Jain and Buddhist faiths.
due to the long period of rule by the Nawabs, the influence of Nawabi art is visible in architecture and aspects of daily life such as cuisine, clothing, and household items

AY4.claim: Ram Navami, Diwali and Kartik Purnima are among Ayodhya's biggest festivals.

evidence.quote: The city is known for its vibrant festivals, including Ram Navami, Diwali, and Kartik Purnima, which are celebrated with great fervour and enthusiasm.

AY5.claim: Maharishi Valmiki International Airport is about 10 km from Ayodhya Dham; Lucknow, Gorakhpur, Prayagraj and Varanasi airports are alternatives.

evidence.quote: Several airlines are operating from Major cities to Maharishi Valmiki International Airport Ayodhya which is approximately 10km from Ayodhya Dham . People can also reach from Lucknow ,Gorakhpur, Prayagraj and Varanasi Airports.

AY6.claim: Ayodhya Cantt and Ayodhya Dham are the main stations; by rail Ayodhya Dham is 135 km from Lucknow and 191 km from Varanasi.

evidence.quote: Ayodhya Cantt and Ayodhya Dham are major railway stations of the district and are well connected to almost all major cities and towns. By Rail route Ayodhya Dham is 135 kms. from Lucknow, 164 kms. from Gorakhpur, 157 kms. from Prayagraj and 191 kms from Varanasi.

AY7.claim: UPSRTC buses run 24 hours; Ayodhya is about 130 km from Lucknow, 160 km from Prayagraj, 200 km from Varanasi and 636 km from Delhi.

evidence.quote: Services of Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation buses are available 24 hours a day
The city is about 130 k.m. from Lucknow, 200 k.m. from Varanasi, 160 k.m. from Prayagraj , 140 k.m. from Gorakhpur and about 636 k.m. from Delhi.

AY8.claim: Five Jain Tirthankaras are believed to have been born in Ayodhya; the Badi Murti temple in Raiganj has a 31-foot marble statue of Rishabhdev.

evidence.quote: Ayodhya is renowned for hosting the sacred events of 18 'Kalyanak' for various 'tirthankars,' including being the birthplace and spiritual teaching ground for five Thirthankars
This impressive temple features a 31-foot marble statue of Rishabhdev.

AY9.claim: Ayodhya has living traditions of Ramlila and temple music; Ramlila troupes still perform in its temples.

evidence.quote: Within the performing arts, Ramlila troupes also perform.

RM1.claim: The Ram Janmabhoomi temple is 161 feet tall including its spire, with 160 columns on the ground floor.

evidence.quote: The total height of the temple including the peak:161 feet
Number of columns in the ground floor of the temple:160

RM2.claim: The temple is built entirely of stone in the Nagara style; the 51-inch Ram Lalla idol stands in the sanctum.

evidence.quote: The Ram Mandir in Ayodhya is made entirely of stone
The 51-inch-tall Ram Lalla idol in the temple's sanctum sanctorum

RM3.claim: The temple trust issues free passes for darshan and aarti and charges no fee for them.

evidence.quote: Trust does not charge any fee for aarti & darshan passes

RM4.claim: The trust lists Mangal Aarti at 4:30 am, Shringar Aarti at 6:30 am and Shayan Aarti at 9:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Mangal Aarti : 04:30 AM
Shringar Aarti : 06:30 AM
Shayan Aarti : 09:30 PM

RM5.claim: The trust office (Ramghat Chauraha, near Manas Bhawan) is open 10 am–6 pm daily; helpdesk 05278-292000.

evidence.quote: Office Timings: 10:00 AM to 06:00 PM (All days)
Helpdesk  Numbers: 05278-292000

AYS1.claim: Hanuman Garhi is 1 km from Ayodhya railway station; its main shrine has an idol of the child Hanuman on his mother Anjani's lap.

evidence.quote: Hanuman Garhi is 1 km from Ayodhya railway station.
You will find here a beautiful idol of Bal (young) sitting on lap of Maa Anjani at the main temple.

AYS2.claim: Tradition holds that Hanuman lived here to guard Ayodhya; the temple is said to have been built by Vikramaditya.

evidence.quote: Vikramaditya got a temple constructed which later on came to be known as Hanuman Garhi. It is believed that Lord Hanuman (Pavan Putra) lived here guard Ayodhya.

AYS3.claim: Kanak Bhawan, north-east of Ram Janmabhoomi, is believed to have been Kaikeyi's gift to Sita; the sanctum holds idols of Ram and Sita.

evidence.quote: Kanak Bhawan is to the north-east of Ram Janam Bhumi, Ramkot, in Ayodhya.
It is believed that this Bhawan was gifted to Devi Sita by Kaikei immediately after her marriage to Lord Ram.
The main idols installed in the garbhgrih (sanctum), are of Lord Ram and Devi Sita.

AYS4.claim: The present Kanak Bhawan was rebuilt by Vrish Bhanu Kunwari.

evidence.quote: Later it was rebuilt/renovated by Vrish Bhanu Kunwari which exists even today.

AYS5.claim: Ram ki Paidi is a series of ghats on the Saryu, floodlit at night, where pilgrims bathe.

evidence.quote: Ram ki Paidi is a series of ghats on the bank of River Saryu. The river front brings forth an outstanding Landscape especially in floodlit night.
These serve as platforms to devotees who it is said, come to wash away their sins by taking a dip in the river.

AYS6.claim: The Nageshwarnath Temple at Ram ki Paidi is said to have been founded by Kush, Rama's son; the present temple dates from 1750, and Mahashivratri draws thousands.

evidence.quote: This temple is at Ram Ki Paidi in Ayodhya. The temple of Nageshwarnath is said to have been established by Kush, the son of Rama.
The present temple was built in 1750 by the minister of Safdar Jung, named Naval Rai.
During the festival time of Mahashivratri the temple receive thousands of devotees.

AYS7.claim: Gulab Bari ('garden of roses') is the tomb of Nawab Shuja-ud-Daula, third Nawab of Awadh, set in a charbagh with fountains and water channels.

evidence.quote: Gulab Bari (literally meaning ‘Garden of Roses’) the Tomb of Nawab Shuja-ud-Daula is in Ayodhya
The tomb proper stands in the centre of a Charbagh Garden accompanied by fountains and shallow water channels.

AYS8.claim: The garden has many varieties of roses set beside water fountains.

evidence.quote: This place has a good collection of roses of various varieties set by the sides of water fountains.

PR1.claim: Prayagraj stands at the confluence of the Ganga, the Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati and is one of the Kumbh Mela cities.

evidence.quote: Prayagraj is a beautiful city situated at the confluence of the Rivers Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswati.
Prayagraj is one of the destinations which holds the Kumbh Mela, world’s largest congregation of devotees.

PR2.claim: Prayagraj was a nerve centre of India's freedom movement and has played a leading role in Hindi and Urdu literature.

evidence.quote: The city was the nerve centre of activities during the India’s Freedom Movement.
Prayagraj has also played a leading role in development of Hindi and Urdu literature.

PR3.claim: British-era landmarks include the University of Allahabad, the High Court and the All Saints Cathedral, designed by Sir William Emerson.

evidence.quote: Some prominent structures in Prayagraj, the erstwhile capital of the United Provinces, are the University of Allahabad and the Allahabad High Court. The All Saints Cathedral is perhaps the finest Anglican cathedral in Asia.
it was designed by Sir William Emerson

PR4.claim: The Magh Mela is held every year from mid-January to mid-February, starting on Makar Sankranti, with a tented township at the Sangam.

evidence.quote: This Mela is held every year during the Hindu month of Magh (corresponding from mid January – mid February) and the important bathing dates are spread over a period of 45 days. It commences on the day of Makar Sankranti in January, which is the first important bathing day.

PR5.claim: Prayagraj's festival year includes a water sports festival in February, Dussehra chowki processions and Deepavali, when diyas float on the rivers at the Sangam.

evidence.quote: The Water Sports Festival (February) organised by the tourism department involves exciting adventure sports such as Kayaking, Canoeing, etc.
The ten-day Dushehra in Prayagraj is known for its Chowkis.
Sangam presents an out of this world on this occasion with thousands of diyas floating on the rivers.

PR6.claim: Prayagraj's Bamrauli airport is about 17 km from Daraganj; Prayagraj Junction, Prayag and Rambagh are the city's stations.

evidence.quote: Bamrauli Airport, Prayagraj - 17 km, Lal Bahadur Shastri Airport, Varanasi - 128 km, Amausi International Airport, Lucknow - 200 km.
Prayagraj Railway Junction - 6 km, Prayag Station - 5.4 km, Rambagh Station - 4 km.

PRS1.claim: At the Sangam the brown Ganga meets the green Yamuna, about 7 km from Civil Lines below the ramparts of Akbar's fort.

evidence.quote: This is the point where the brown water of the Ganga meets the green water of the Yamuna, along with the mythical Saraswati, which remains unseen but believed to run underground. It is located about 7 km from Civil Lines, overlooked by the eastern ramparts of the Akbar Fort.

PRS2.claim: Boats to the Sangam can be hired at the ghat near the fort; priests on mid-river platforms help pilgrims with their ritual bath.

evidence.quote: At the mid-river point priests perch on small platforms to perform puja and assist the devout in their ritual ablutions in the shallow waters.
Boats to the Sangam can be rented by pilgrims and tourists alike at the ghat near the fort.

PRS3.claim: The Kumbh is held at the Sangam once every twelve years; it is the largest religious congregation in India.

evidence.quote: here the Kumbh is held once in every twelve years, which is the greatest and holiest of all.
The Maha Kumbh Mela is the largest religious congregation in India, attended by millions.

PRS4.claim: Incredible India lists the Sangam as open 5 am to 7 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 05:00 AM
Closing time - 07:00 PM

PRS5.claim: Anand Bhawan, built by Motilal Nehru, is a house museum of the Nehru family and has the Jawahar Planetarium.

evidence.quote: The Anand Bhawan is a historic house museum in Allahabad, which belongs to the Nehru family.
The Bhawan houses the Jawahar Planetarium.

PRS6.claim: Next door, Swaraj Bhawan was the original Nehru mansion, where Indira Gandhi was born; it was given to the Indian National Congress in the 1920s.

evidence.quote: It served as the ancestral home of the Nehru family, Prime Minister, Indira Gandhi was born here. In the 1920s, Motilal Nehru donated the house to the Indian National Congress

PRS7.claim: Khusro Bagh is a walled garden with three sandstone Mughal tombs: Prince Khusro (Jahangir's eldest son), his mother Shah Begum and his sister.

evidence.quote: Khusro Bagh is a large historical garden, in which tombs of Prince Khusro, the eldest son of Emperor Jahangir and Sultan Begum are located. The three sandstone mausoleums within this walled garden, represent an exquisite example of Mughal architecture.
Next to the Begum’s tomb is the tomb of Khusrau’s sister, Nithar.

PRS8.claim: Nithar's mausoleum, the most elaborate of the three, has rooms with ceilings painted with stars.

evidence.quote: Architecturally, this is the most elaborate of the three.
Within the plinth are rooms, whose ceilings have been elaborately painted with stars in concentric circles.

PRS9.claim: The Allahabad Museum in Chandrashekhar Azad Park (Company Bagh) shows sculpture, paintings, coins and manuscripts in sixteen galleries.

evidence.quote: The Allahabad Museum is centrally located in the Civil Lines area of the city in a lush green garden at Chandrashekhar Azad Park, popularly known as Company Bagh.
The artefacts are displayed in sixteen different galleries

PRS10.claim: Its collections include personalia of Gandhi, Nehru and Allahabad's Hindi writers.

evidence.quote: personalia collections pertaining to Gandhi, Nehru and Literary personalities of Allahabad like Sumitra Nandan Pant,Suryakant Tripathi “Nirala”, Premchand, and Mahadevi Verma

PRS11.claim: Near the Sangam in Daraganj, the Lete Hue (reclining) Hanuman temple has a 20-foot south-facing idol of Hanuman lying down.

evidence.quote: It is believed that this strange statue of Hanuman is south-facing and 20 feet long.
he lay down here on the banks of the Sangam

MT1.claim: Mathura, on the Yamuna, is revered as the birthplace of Krishna and is one of Hinduism's seven holy cities; with Vrindavan it forms the heart of Braj.

evidence.quote: Situated on the banks of the river Yamuna in Uttar Pradesh, the sacred city of Mathura
Renowned as the birthplace of Lord Krishna, Mathura is one of Hinduism's seven holy cities
Mathura, along with its twin city Vrindavan (Krishna's spiritual abode), forms the heart of Braj Bhoomi.

MT2.claim: Mathura is about 145 km south-east of Delhi and 58 km north-west of Agra.

evidence.quote: It is located at a distance of 145 km to south-east of Delhi, and almost 58 km to north-west of Agra.

MT3.claim: The nearest airport is Agra's Kheria Airport; Mathura Junction and Mathura Cantt are on the busy Delhi–Agra rail route, and the city is linked to Delhi by the Noida–Agra expressway.

evidence.quote: Railway Station(s): Mathura Junction (MTJ), Mathura Cantt. (MRT)

Nearest airport to Mathura is in Agra, which is around 57.9 km far from this place. Mathura is a major railway junction, which is connected by many trains operating on routes between Delhi and Agra on regular basis. Mathura is well-linked with New Delhi through Noida-Agra express way.

MT4.claim: Vishram Ghat is the most important of Mathura's 25 ghats, where Krishna is believed to have rested after defeating Kansa.

evidence.quote: The Vishram Ghat (ghat of rest) is the most significant among the city's twenty-five ghats. Here, Krishna is believed to have rested after vanquishing his demon maternal uncle Kansa.

MT5.claim: Mathura's Government Museum holds Mauryan and Kushan-era sculpture, pottery and coins; Mathura was an early centre of devotional sculpture for Buddhism, Jainism and Hinduism.

evidence.quote: Step into the Government Museum and be transported through time. Here, a treasure trove of archaeological wonders awaits from the Mauryan and Kushan periods
This city became the "first artistic centre to produce devotional icons for all three faiths,"

MT6.claim: October to March has pleasant weather; Janmashtami (August/September) and Holi (March) are the most festive times.

evidence.quote: Plan your visit between October and March, when pleasant weather graces the city. To truly immerse yourself in the vibrant spirit of Mathura, consider coming during Krishna Janmashtami (August/September) or Holi (March)

MT7.claim: Mathura and Vrindavan are vegetarian holy cities known for pedas, kachori and bedhai, makhan mishri and lassi; meat and alcohol are forbidden.

evidence.quote: As these cities are considered holy spaces, meat and alcohol are forbidden here, while vegetarian restaurants offering Mathura Peda, Lal Peda, Makhan Mishri Jalebi Bedhai, and Poori Sabji are special treats that await.

MT8.claim: Chowk Bazaar, Holi Gate and the area around the Dwarkadhish Temple are Mathura's street-food streets.

evidence.quote: Popular areas offering street food in Mathura include Chowk Bazaar, Holi Gate and Dwarkadhish Temple

MT9.claim: In Braj, 'Radhe Radhe' is the everyday greeting.

evidence.quote: Here, a simple "Radhe Radhe!" (pronounced rah-day rah-day) isn't just a hello

MT10.claim: Gokul, where Krishna is believed to have grown up, is about 10 km away; Govardhan Hill is about 25 km from Mathura.

evidence.quote: Just 10 km away lies Gokul
A pilgrimage to Govardhan, roughly 25 km from Mathura, is a must for any Krishna devotee.

MT11.claim: Raslila and Rasiya songs are central to Braj culture, sung at Holi and other festivals.

evidence.quote: Raaslila is another predominant form of Mathura culture.
These songs are compulsorily sung in Holi celebrations and all other festive occasions at Braj.

MTS1.claim: The Krishna Janmasthan complex is built around the prison cell where Krishna is believed to have been born.

evidence.quote: The temple is built around the prison cell where Krishna is said to have been born.

MTS2.claim: Photography is banned inside the Janmasthan complex.

evidence.quote: Photography is banned inside the complex by the government.

MTS3.claim: Next to the prison cell stands a temple to the eight-armed goddess Yogmaya.

evidence.quote: Adjacent to the entrance of the prison cell, stands the temple where Astabhuja Maa Yogmaya manifested.

MTS4.claim: The Dwarkadhish Temple, one of Mathura's oldest and largest, was built in 1814 by Seth Gokul Das Parikh, treasurer of Gwalior State.

evidence.quote: Sri Dwarkadheesh Mandir   is one of the oldest and largest temples of Mathura city
its current structure was built up by Seth Gokul Das Parikh, the treasurer of then Gwalior State(Scindia) in 1814

MTS5.claim: Krishna is worshipped here as Dwarkadhish in black marble, beside a white marble image of Radha.

evidence.quote: There the main deity is of Lord Dwarkadheesh, a form of Lord Krishna seen in a black Marble idol named Dwarkanath. With him is the White marble idol of his counterpart deity Sri Radharani.

VR1.claim: Vrindavan, Mathura's twin town, is associated with Krishna's youth and is crowded with temples and ashrams.

evidence.quote: Just a short drive away is Vrindavan, synonymous with Krishna's playful youth. Vrindavan is dotted with temples and ashrams associated with Lord Krishna and his beloved consort, Radha.

VR2.claim: The Banke Bihari Temple and the ISKCON temple are Vrindavan's most visited.

evidence.quote: The Banke Bihari Temple and the ISKCON Temple are among the most visited attractions here.

VR3.claim: Cheer Ghat is one of Vrindavan's holiest bathing ghats.

evidence.quote: In Vrindavan, don’t miss Cheer Ghat, one of the holiest bathing sites.

VRS1.claim: At Banke Bihari, priests regularly draw a curtain across the idol.

evidence.quote: At the Banke Bihari temple, Krishna's idol is so enchanting that priests regularly draw a curtain to prevent devotees from being overwhelmed by its beauty.

VRS2.claim: The image of Krishna stands in the tribhanga ('bent in three places') posture; it was first worshipped by Swami Haridas at Nidhivan.

evidence.quote: Bankey Bihari Ji was originally worshipped at Nidhivana.
The image of Lord Krishna stands in the Tribhanga posture.

VRS3.claim: Makhan mishri — butter with sugar candy — is served daily as prasad at Banke Bihari.

evidence.quote: Makhan Mishri was Lord Krishna's favourite dish in Mathura and Vrindavan, served daily at Banke Bihari Temple of Vrindavan as part of its Prasad distributions.

VRS4.claim: Prem Mandir stands on a 54-acre site on the outskirts of Vrindavan, dedicated to Radha Krishna and Sita Ram; it opened to the public on 17 February 2012.

evidence.quote: The complex is on a 54-acre site on the outskirts of Vrindavan, and is dedicated to Lord Radha Krishna and Sita Ram.
The temple was opened to public on 17 February.

VRS5.claim: Prem Mandir was established by Kripalu Maharaj and is maintained by Jagadguru Kripalu Parishat.

evidence.quote: It is maintained by Jagadguru Kripalu Parishat
The temple structure was established by the fifth Jagadguru, Kripalu Maharaj.

VRS6.claim: The Sri Krishna Balaram Mandir at Raman Reti, built in 1975, was the first temple built by ISKCON; Swami Prabhupada laid its foundation.

evidence.quote: Sri Krishna Balrama Temple is acknowledged for being the first temple constructed by the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON). Built in 1975 by the ISKCON cult, the foundation of the shrine was laid by Swami Prabhupada (founder of ISKCON) himself. Located at Raman Reti in Vrindavan

BR1.claim: Barsana, about 40 km from Mathura, is believed to be Radha's birthplace and is set around two hills, Brahma and Vishnu.

evidence.quote: Barsana lies 40 km from Mathura, it is a hallowed town situated around two hills, Brahma Hill and Vishnu Hill.
Barsana is believed to be the town where Radha was born

BR2.claim: The Radha Rani Temple is Barsana's main attraction.

evidence.quote: The main attraction of the town is the historical Radha Rani Temple which attracts huge number of devotees.

BR3.claim: Lathmar Holi falls in February or March and spans two days: Nandgaon's men come to Barsana, then Barsana's women go to Nandgaon.

evidence.quote: In the months of February or March, the people of Barsana celebrate the renowned Lathmar Holi.

This sacred celebration spans two days - the first seeing the villagers of Nandgaon (Krishna’s village) arrive in Barsana to rejoice at the Radharani temple, and on the next day, Barsana's Gopis (girls) journeying to Nandgaon to partake in the ritual.

BR4.claim: Women playfully beat the men with bamboo sticks while Holi songs are sung.

evidence.quote: As Holi songs echo through the air, you get to witness a unique and fun tradition, with women lovingly wielding bamboo sticks to shower affectionate 'beatings' upon the men.

BR5.claim: Radhashtami, Radha's birthday, is celebrated in July or August.

evidence.quote: Another occasion when you can witness the zenith of Barsana's spiritual celebration is the auspicious Radhashtami festival, celebrated in July or August.

LK1.claim: Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh's capital, lies on the Gomti river and flowered under the Nawabs of Awadh, especially Asaf-ud-Daula (1775–1797).

evidence.quote: Nestled along the tranquil banks of the Gomti River, this capital city of Uttar Pradesh
Lucknow blossomed into a city known for its architectural splendour and cultural diversity under the Nawabs of Awadh, especially the visionary Asaf-ud-Daula, who reigned from 1775 to 1797.

LK2.claim: Asaf-ud-Daula moved the capital of Awadh from Faizabad to Lucknow in 1775.

evidence.quote: the later Nawab Asaf-ud-daulah’s decision to relocate the capital to Lucknow in 1775 elevated the city to its esteemed status as a capital

LK3.claim: Lucknow is known for its tehzeeb (etiquette), Kathak dance, music and poetry.

evidence.quote: Art and culture are at the heart of Lucknow's 'tehzeeb' (etiquette) and 'adab' (sophistication). The city is celebrated for its classical dance form Kathak, its traditional music, and its rich literary traditions.

LK4.claim: Awadhi cuisine is Lucknow's pride: galouti and Tunday kebabs, Lucknowi biryani, and sweets in the Chowk.

evidence.quote: From the succulent Galouti Kebabs to the aromatic splendour of Lucknawi Biryani
Among Lucknow's culinary treasures are the famous Tunday Kabab which are cooked to perfection on charcoal fires

LK5.claim: Chikankari hand embroidery is Lucknow's signature craft, sold in its markets along with zardozi.

evidence.quote: Chikankari, a delicate and traditional hand embroidery craft, represents a vital facet of Uttar Pradesh's artistic heritage, predominantly practiced in Lucknow.

LK6.claim: Lucknow has made attars (perfumes) since the 19th century — khus, keora, chameli and others.

evidence.quote: For those seeking fragrant delights, Lucknow has been producing 'attars' or perfumes since the 19th century.

LK7.claim: Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport is at Amausi, 14 km from the city centre, with direct flights to many Indian cities and the Gulf.

evidence.quote: Situated in Amausi, 14 kilometers from the city’s nucleus, this airport was formerly known as Amausi Airport.
International connections to: Muscat, Dammam, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Jeddah, Sharjah, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, and Ras-al-Khaymah.

LK8.claim: Charbagh is Lucknow's largest and busiest railway station, next to Lucknow Junction.

places.name: Ayodhya
places.summary: The city on the Saryu revered as Lord Rama's birthplace: the new Ram Janmabhoomi temple, Hanuman Garhi, Kanak Bhawan and lamp-lit ghats.
places.seoTitle: Ayodhya Travel Guide: Ram Mandir, Temples & How to Reach
places.seoDescription: Plan a trip to Ayodhya: the Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir and free darshan passes, Hanuman Garhi, Kanak Bhawan, Ram ki Paidi ghats, festivals and how to get there.

images.alt: Priests performing the evening aarti on a ghat by the Saryu river in Ayodhya
images.caption: Evening aarti on the Saryu, Ayodhya

overview.text:
Ayodhya sits on the banks of the Sarayu (Saryu) river and is revered by millions of Hindus as the birthplace of Lord Rama. In ancient times it was the capital of the Kosala kingdom, and today it is one of India's busiest pilgrimage cities, centred on the new Shri Ram Janmabhoomi temple.

There is more to Ayodhya than one temple. Hanuman Garhi, Kanak Bhawan and the Nageshwarnath Temple are each tied to stories from the Ramayana; Ram ki Paidi's ghats glow on the river after dark; and Gulab Bari, the rose-garden tomb of Nawab Shuja-ud-Daula, is a reminder of the city's Nawabi past. The district's own account of its culture notes Vaishnava, Shaiva, Jain and Buddhist influences — five Jain Tirthankaras are believed to have been born here — and Ramlila troupes still perform in the temples.

Most visitors come for a day or two. Go early in the morning for the main temples, and come back to the river in the evening.

items.body: Darshan at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir — passes are free.
Hanuman Garhi, the hilltop temple of Ayodhya's guardian.
Kanak Bhawan, believed to be the palace gifted to Sita.
Ram ki Paidi's floodlit ghats on the Saryu after dark.
Gulab Bari, a Nawab's tomb in a rose garden.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Maharishi Valmiki International Airport is about 10 km from Ayodhya Dham; you can also fly into Lucknow, Gorakhpur, Prayagraj or Varanasi.

By train: Ayodhya Dham and Ayodhya Cantt are the main stations. By rail Ayodhya Dham is 135 km from Lucknow, 157 km from Prayagraj and 191 km from Varanasi.

By road: UPSRTC buses run round the clock. Ayodhya is about 130 km from Lucknow, 160 km from Prayagraj, 200 km from Varanasi and 636 km from Delhi.

best_time.text: Ram Navami, Diwali and Kartik Purnima are Ayodhya's biggest festivals — spectacular, but also the most crowded days of the year. For an easier visit, come outside these dates and start early, before the heat and the queues build. Across Uttar Pradesh, summer brings hot winds called loo, and the south-west monsoon brings most of the year's rain.

places.name: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir
places.summary: Ayodhya's new stone temple at Rama's birthplace, 161 feet tall, with the 51-inch Ram Lalla idol — darshan and aarti passes are free.
places.seoTitle: Ram Mandir Ayodhya: Darshan Passes, Aarti Times & Tips
places.seoDescription: Visit the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir in Ayodhya: free darshan and aarti passes, aarti timings, temple facts, helpdesk number and practical tips.

images.alt: The carved pink sandstone Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir decorated with marigold garlands, with flowerbeds in front, Ayodhya
images.caption: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir, January 2024

overview.text:
The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir stands at the site revered as the birthplace of Lord Rama and is now the spiritual centre of Ayodhya. The temple is built entirely of stone in the Nagara style and rises 161 feet including its spire; the ground floor alone has 160 columns.

In the sanctum stands the 51-inch Ram Lalla idol. The temple is run by the Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra trust, which issues free passes for darshan and for the daily aartis — it charges no fee for them. Expect queues and security checks, especially on festival days, and give yourself a few hours.

places.name: Hanuman Garhi
places.summary: Ayodhya's hilltop Hanuman temple, 1 km from the station, where the child Hanuman sits in his mother Anjani's lap.
places.seoTitle: Hanuman Garhi Ayodhya: Temple Guide & Visiting Tips
places.seoDescription: Hanuman Garhi in Ayodhya: the legend of Hanuman guarding the city, the idol of Bal Hanuman with Maa Anjani, and how to fit it into a day of temples.

images.commons: File:Hanuman Garhi Temple, a major religious site in Ayodhya utter pradesh.jpg
images.alt: The red-spired Hanuman Garhi temple above a crowded street in Ayodhya
images.caption: Hanuman Garhi, Ayodhya

overview.text:
Hanuman Garhi is one of Ayodhya's most visited temples, about 1 km from Ayodhya railway station. Tradition holds that Lord Hanuman lived here to guard Ayodhya, and that a temple was first built on the spot by King Vikramaditya.

The main shrine has an idol of Bal (the child) Hanuman sitting in the lap of his mother, Maa Anjani. Many pilgrims visit Hanuman Garhi before going on to the Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir — greeting the city's guardian first. Climb the steps early in the morning, when the crowds are thinner and the temple bells and chanting fill the lanes below.

items.body: Go early in the morning to avoid the longest queues.
Watch your bags and glasses — monkeys are bold around temples in Ayodhya.
It is a short walk from here to Kanak Bhawan and the Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir.

places.name: Kanak Bhawan
places.summary: One of Ayodhya's finest temples, believed to be the palace Kaikeyi gave to Sita, with idols of Ram and Sita in the sanctum.
places.seoTitle: Kanak Bhawan Ayodhya: Sita's Palace Temple Guide
places.seoDescription: Kanak Bhawan in Ayodhya: the legend of Sita's palace, the idols of Ram and Sita, its location by Ram Janmabhoomi and tips for your visit.

images.caption: Kanak Bhawan

overview.text:
Kanak Bhawan stands north-east of Ram Janmabhoomi in the Ramkot area and is one of Ayodhya's finest and best-known temples. Tradition says this was the palace that Queen Kaikeyi gave to Sita straight after her marriage to Rama — the private home of Sita and Rama.

The building was renovated by Vikramaditya and later rebuilt by Vrish Bhanu Kunwari; that structure still stands today. In the sanctum, the main idols are of Rama and Sita. Kanak Bhawan is quieter and more intimate than the big temples nearby, and it is worth lingering in its courtyard.

items.body: It is close to the Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir, so visit both in one morning.
Dress modestly and leave footwear outside.

places.name: Ram ki Paidi
places.summary: A chain of ghats on the Saryu where pilgrims bathe, floodlit at night, with the Nageshwarnath Temple said to have been founded by Rama's son Kush.
places.seoTitle: Ram ki Paidi Ayodhya: Ghats, Evening Lights & Temples
places.seoDescription: Ram ki Paidi in Ayodhya: the floodlit ghats on the Saryu, the Nageshwarnath Temple, Mahashivratri crowds and the best time to visit.

images.alt: The ghats of Ram ki Paidi lit up in colour at night beside the Saryu in Ayodhya
images.caption: Ram ki Paidi at night

overview.text:
Ram ki Paidi is a series of ghats along the River Saryu. Pilgrims come to bathe here, believing a dip washes away their sins, and the riverfront is at its most striking when it is floodlit at night.

On the ghats stands the Nageshwarnath Temple, which tradition says was founded by Kush, the son of Rama. Legend tells that Kush lost his armlet while bathing in the Saryu; it was found by a serpent maiden who was a devotee of Shiva, and he built the temple for her. The present temple dates from 1750, and Mahashivratri brings thousands of devotees.

items.body: Come after sunset to see the ghats floodlit.
Expect very large crowds at the Nageshwarnath Temple on Mahashivratri.

items.body: A chain of bathing ghats on the Saryu

places.seoDescription: Gulab Bari, Ayodhya: the tomb of Nawab Shuja-ud-Daula, third Nawab of Awadh, in a Mughal charbagh garden of roses and fountains.

images.alt: The domed tomb of Gulab Bari at the end of a garden path lined with hedges in Ayodhya
images.caption: Gulab Bari

overview.text:
Gulab Bari — literally the 'garden of roses' — is the tomb of Nawab Shuja-ud-Daula, the third Nawab of Awadh. The domed tomb stands at the centre of a charbagh garden laid out with fountains and shallow water channels, and the garden is planted with many varieties of roses beside its fountains.

It is a calm counterpoint to Ayodhya's temples and a reminder that the city was once at the heart of the Nawabs' Awadh, before the capital moved to Lucknow. Locals also treat it as a holy place.

items.body: Come in the cool of the morning or late afternoon, when the garden is at its best.

places.name: Prayagraj
places.summary: The city at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna: the Triveni Sangam, the Magh and Kumbh Melas, Anand Bhawan and Mughal Khusro Bagh.
places.seoTitle: Prayagraj Travel Guide: Sangam, Magh Mela & Places to Visit
places.seoDescription: Plan a trip to Prayagraj (Allahabad): Triveni Sangam boat rides, Magh and Kumbh Mela dates, Anand Bhawan, Khusro Bagh, the museum and how to get there.

images.alt: Rowing boats with pilgrims on the calm water of the Sangam at Prayagraj at dusk
images.caption: Boats at the Sangam, Prayagraj

overview.text:
Prayagraj — long known as Allahabad — sits where the Ganga and the Yamuna meet, joined in belief by the hidden Saraswati. This confluence, the Triveni Sangam, makes it one of the holiest places in Hinduism and one of the four cities that host the Kumbh Mela.

It is also a city of history. Prayagraj was a nerve centre of the freedom movement — the Nehru family's Anand Bhawan is now a museum — and it played a leading role in Hindi and Urdu literature. The British left the University of Allahabad, the High Court and the All Saints Cathedral, while the Mughals left the tombs of Khusro Bagh.

Every winter the Magh Mela fills the riverbanks with a tented city of pilgrims; outside the melas, the Sangam is calmer and easier to enjoy by boat.

items.body: A boat ride to the Triveni Sangam.
Anand Bhawan, the Nehru family home.
Khusro Bagh's three Mughal tombs.
The Allahabad Museum's sixteen galleries.
The reclining Hanuman temple near the Sangam.

how_to_reach.text: Prayagraj's Bamrauli airport is about 17 km from Daraganj, near the Sangam; Varanasi's airport is about 128 km away and Lucknow's about 200 km. Prayagraj Junction is the main railway station, with Prayag and Rambagh stations closer to the river.

best_time.text: The Magh Mela runs every year from mid-January to mid-February, starting on Makar Sankranti, with important bathing dates over 45 days; a tented township rises at the Sangam. February also brings the tourism department's water sports festival, Dussehra is known for its chowki processions, and at Deepavali diyas float on the rivers at the Sangam. Summer is hot, with dry loo winds; most rain falls in the monsoon.

items.title: When is the Magh Mela?
items.body: Every year in the Hindu month of Magh, roughly mid-January to mid-February, starting on Makar Sankranti.

items.title: How often is the Kumbh held at Prayagraj?
items.body: The Kumbh is held at the Sangam once every twelve years.

items.title: How do I get to the Sangam?

Agree the boat fare before you set off.

places.name: Triveni Sangam
places.summary: The holy confluence of the brown Ganga and green Yamuna, reached by boat from the ghat below Akbar's fort; home of the Kumbh and Magh Melas.
places.seoTitle: Triveni Sangam Prayagraj: Boat Ride, Timings & Kumbh
places.seoDescription: Visit the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj: where the Ganga meets the Yamuna, hiring a boat, ritual bathing, hours, the Kumbh and Magh Mela, and the reclining Hanuman temple.

images.alt: A wooden boat full of pilgrims on the Triveni Sangam at Prayagraj
images.caption: Pilgrims at the Triveni Sangam

overview.text:
The Triveni Sangam is where the brown water of the Ganga meets the green water of the Yamuna — and, in belief, the unseen Saraswati, said to flow underground. It lies about 7 km from Civil Lines, overlooked by the eastern ramparts of Akbar's fort.

Boats can be hired at the ghat near the fort. At the meeting point, priests sit on small platforms in the shallow water to perform puja and help pilgrims with their ritual bath. Once every twelve years the Kumbh is held here — India's largest religious gathering — and every winter the Magh Mela fills the banks with tents.

Near the Sangam in Daraganj, the Lete Hue Hanuman temple has a rare 20-foot idol of Hanuman lying down, south-facing.

items.title: Hours
items.body: 5 am to 7 pm, as listed by Incredible India.

items.title: Boats
items.body: Hire at the ghat near the fort; agree the fare first.
Go at sunrise for calm water and soft light.
During the Magh Mela and Kumbh, expect huge crowds and follow police directions.

places.name: Anand Bhawan
places.summary: The Nehru family home in Prayagraj, now a house museum with the Jawahar Planetarium; Swaraj Bhawan next door is where Indira Gandhi was born.
places.seoTitle: Anand Bhawan Prayagraj: Nehru House Museum Guide
places.seoDescription: Visit Anand Bhawan in Prayagraj: the Nehru family house museum, Swaraj Bhawan where Indira Gandhi was born, the Jawahar Planetarium and nearby sights.

images.commons: File:Front Anand Bhawan Allahabad Dec23 A7C 08485.jpg
images.alt: The white two-storey Anand Bhawan with its domed tower and verandahs in Prayagraj
images.caption: Anand Bhawan

overview.text:
Anand Bhawan is a historic house museum that belonged to the Nehru family. It was built by Motilal Nehru as the family's home after their original mansion, Swaraj Bhawan, became the local headquarters of the Indian National Congress, and it houses the Jawahar Planetarium.

Swaraj Bhawan, in the same complex, was the ancestral home of the Nehrus and the birthplace of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi; Motilal Nehru gave it to the Congress in the 1920s, and it became a launch pad for key moments of the independence movement. Together they make one of the most personal places in India to understand the freedom struggle.

items.body: Pair it with the Allahabad Museum, which also displays Gandhi and Nehru memorabilia.
Families can add a show at the Jawahar Planetarium.

overview.text:
Khusro Bagh is a large walled garden holding the tombs of Prince Khusro, the eldest son of Emperor Jahangir, of his mother and of his sister. The three sandstone mausoleums are a fine example of Mughal architecture.

The tomb of Khusro's sister, Nithar, is the most elaborate of the three: inside its raised plinth are rooms whose ceilings are painted with stars in concentric circles. Khusro himself rebelled against his father, was imprisoned in this garden and was later killed — a sad story behind a peaceful place.

items.body: Look up inside Nithar's tomb for the painted star ceilings.

places.name: Mathura
places.summary: Krishna's birthplace on the Yamuna: the Janmasthan complex, Dwarkadhish Temple, Vishram Ghat, Kushan sculpture and the sweets of Braj.

images.caption: Vishram Ghat, Mathura

overview.text:
Mathura sits on the banks of the Yamuna and is revered as the birthplace of Lord Krishna — one of Hinduism's seven holy cities. Together with its twin town Vrindavan it forms the heart of Braj, the land of Krishna's childhood.

The Shri Krishna Janmasthan complex is built around the prison cell where Krishna is believed to have been born, and the Dwarkadhish Temple, built in 1814, is one of the city's oldest and largest. Vishram Ghat, the most important of Mathura's 25 ghats, is where Krishna is said to have rested after defeating Kansa.

Mathura was also an early centre of sculpture: its Government Museum holds Mauryan and Kushan-era works from a time when the city made devotional images for Buddhism, Jainism and Hinduism. Come hungry — Mathura's pedas, kachori and lassi are famous, and the city is vegetarian.

best_time.text: October to March is the most pleasant time to visit. For the festivals, come at Janmashtami (August or September) or Holi (March) — Barsana's Lathmar Holi, in February or March, is one of a kind. The summer months bring hot loo winds.

places.summary: Mathura's temple complex built around the prison cell where Krishna is believed to have been born, with the shrine of eight-armed Yogmaya.

overview.text:
The Shri Krishna Janmasthan complex is built around the prison cell where Lord Krishna is believed to have been born to Devaki and Vasudeva, prisoners of the tyrant Kansa. For devotees, standing in this small cell is the emotional heart of any visit to Mathura.

Next to the entrance of the prison cell is a temple to the eight-armed goddess Yogmaya. The complex holds several other shrines to different aspects of Krishna's life. Photography is banned inside, so leave your camera behind and simply take in the atmosphere.

places.name: Dwarkadhish Temple, Mathura
places.summary: Mathura's grand temple of 1814, where Krishna is worshipped as the king of Dwarka in black marble beside a white marble Radha.
places.seoTitle: Dwarkadhish Temple Mathura: History, Idols & Visiting Tips

overview.text:
The Dwarkadhish Temple is one of the oldest and largest temples in Mathura. Its present structure was built in 1814 by Seth Gokul Das Parikh, the treasurer of Gwalior State, and it is dedicated to Krishna as Dwarkadhish — the king of Dwarka, where he went to live after leaving Mathura.

The main idol, Dwarkanath, is in black marble, with a white marble image of Radha beside him. Look up at the painted courtyard and carved balconies. The lanes around the temple are among Mathura's best for street food, and Vishram Ghat is a short walk away.

overview.text:
Vrindavan, a short drive from Mathura, is associated with Krishna's playful youth and is crowded with temples and ashrams devoted to Krishna and Radha. Mathura and Vrindavan together form the heart of Braj.

The Banke Bihari Temple and the ISKCON temple are the town's most visited. Banke Bihari is famous for the curtain priests draw across the idol; ISKCON's Krishna Balaram Mandir, built in 1975, was the society's first temple; and Prem Mandir, on a 54-acre site on the edge of town, glows with colour after dark. Cheer Ghat is one of the holiest bathing places on the Yamuna. Like Mathura, Vrindavan is vegetarian and alcohol-free.

places.name: Banke Bihari Temple
places.summary: Vrindavan's best-loved Krishna temple, where the tribhanga idol is hidden by a curtain every few moments and makhan mishri is the prasad.

places.seoDescription: Banke Bihari Temple in Vrindavan: the curtained darshan, the tribhanga Krishna first worshipped by Swami Haridas, makhan mishri prasad and crowd tips.

overview.text:
The Banke Bihari Temple is the most visited in Vrindavan. Its image of Krishna stands in the tribhanga posture — 'bent in three places' — and was first worshipped by Swami Haridas at Nidhivan under the name Kunj-Bihari.

Darshan here is unusual: the priests regularly draw a curtain across the idol, so devotees glimpse Krishna in short moments. Makhan mishri — butter with sugar candy — is offered and distributed as prasad every day. The temple lanes are narrow and the crowds dense; go with patience.

Prem Mandir stands on a 54-acre site on the outskirts of Vrindavan and is dedicated to Radha Krishna and Sita Ram. It was established by Kripalu Maharaj and is maintained by Jagadguru Kripalu Parishat; it opened to the public on 17 February 2012.

Figures of Krishna and his companions, depicting scenes from his life, cover the main temple and fill the gardens. The temple is at its most spectacular after dark, when it is lit in changing colours — plan to arrive before sunset and stay for the lights.

places.summary: ISKCON's first temple, built in 1975 at Raman Reti, where Krishna and Balarama are said to have herded cows on the Yamuna's banks.

places.seoDescription: ISKCON Vrindavan's Sri Krishna Balaram Mandir: the society's first temple (1975), founded by Swami Prabhupada at Raman Reti, and tips for aarti and kirtan.

images.caption: Krishna Balaram Mandir, ISKCON Vrindavan

overview.text:
The Sri Krishna Balaram Mandir, known to everyone as the ISKCON temple, was the first temple built by the International Society for Krishna Consciousness. It was built in 1975 at Raman Reti in Vrindavan, and its foundation was laid by the society's founder, Swami Prabhupada, himself.

Tradition places it where Krishna and his brother Balarama herded cows by the Yamuna. Along with Banke Bihari, it is one of Vrindavan's most visited temples — come for an aarti and the kirtan that fills its white marble courtyard.

overview.text:
Barsana lies about 40 km from Mathura, a town built around two hills, Brahma Hill and Vishnu Hill. It is believed to be the birthplace of Radha, and every lane is tied to stories of Radha and Krishna.

The Radha Rani Temple, on the hilltop, is the main attraction and draws huge numbers of devotees. Barsana is at its most alive during its festivals: Lathmar Holi in February or March, and Radhashtami, Radha's birthday, in July or August.

places.name: Lathmar Holi in Barsana and Nandgaon
places.summary: Two days of Braj Holi in February–March, when Barsana's women playfully beat Nandgaon's men with bamboo sticks to Holi songs.
places.seoTitle: Lathmar Holi Barsana: Dates, What Happens & Tips
places.seoDescription: Experience Lathmar Holi in Barsana and Nandgaon: when it happens, how the two-day festival works, what to expect and tips for visitors.

overview.text:
Lathmar Holi is Braj's most famous Holi. It is celebrated in February or March and acts out the playful teasing between Krishna and Radha's companions: women wield bamboo sticks and shower affectionate 'beatings' on the men, who shield themselves, while Holi songs fill the air.

It spans two days. On the first, the men of Nandgaon — Krishna's village — come to Barsana to celebrate at the Radha Rani Temple; on the next, Barsana's women go to Nandgaon. Rasiya songs, the love songs of Radha and Krishna, are sung throughout.

items.body: Wear old clothes and protect your camera and phone from colour.

places.name: Lucknow
places.summary: The Nawabs' capital on the Gomti: the Bara and Chota Imambaras, Rumi Darwaza, the Residency, Awadhi kebabs and chikankari.

images.alt: The Asafi Mosque with its domes and tall minaret in the Bara Imambara complex, Lucknow

overview.text:
Lucknow, the capital of Uttar Pradesh, lies on the Gomti river. It flowered under the Nawabs of Awadh — above all Asaf-ud-Daula, who moved his capital here from Faizabad in 1775 and reigned until 1797 — and its monuments blend Mughal, Persian and British styles.

The old city's great buildings cluster together in Husainabad: the Bara Imambara with its vast vaulted hall and Bhul Bhulaiya maze, the Rumi Darwaza, the chandelier-filled Chota Imambara and the 221-foot clock tower. A short ride away, the ruined Residency recalls the 1857 siege.

Lucknow is just as famous for its tehzeeb — its courtesy — for Kathak, poetry and music, and for Awadhi food: galouti kebabs, biryani and sweets in the Chowk. Take home chikankari embroidery or a bottle of attar.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport is at Amausi, 14 km from the city centre, with flights across India and to the Gulf and South-East Asia.

By train: Charbagh is the city's largest and busiest station, next to Lucknow Junction.

By road: the Agra and Purvanchal expressways link Lucknow with Agra and eastern UP. Interstate buses use the Alambagh terminal, which has its own metro platform.

local_transport.text: Lucknow has a Metro, and the Alambagh bus terminal connects straight to it. For the old city's monuments, take an app cab or auto to Husainabad and explore on foot — the Bara Imambara, Rumi Darwaza, Chota Imambara and clock tower are close together.

best_time.text: Lucknow has cool, dry winters from late November to February — the best time for sightseeing and for winter treats like malai makhan. Summers, from late March to early June, are hot and sunny, and the monsoon brings most of the rain.

places.name: Bara Imambara
places.summary: Asaf-ud-Daula's famine-relief Imambara (1784–1791) with the world's largest vaulted hall, the Bhul Bhulaiya maze and the Asafi Mosque.
places.seoTitle: Bara Imambara Lucknow: Bhul Bhulaiya, History & Tips
places.seoDescription: Visit Lucknow's Bara (Asafi) Imambara: the famine-relief story, the largest vaulted hall without beams, the Bhul Bhulaiya labyrinth, the mosque and nearby Rumi Darwaza.

images.alt: The Bara Imambara's long façade and lawns seen from above, with a white mosque dome behind, Lucknow
images.caption: Bara Imambara

overview.text:
The Bara Imambara — also called the Asafi Imambara — was built between 1784 and 1791 by Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula during a devastating famine, as a project to give work and food to the people. Its central hall is the largest vaulted hall in the world, roofed without wooden or metal supports.

Above the hall winds the Bhul Bhulaiya, a famous labyrinth of passages. The complex rises through two courts to a mosque flanked by twin minarets, with views over the old city. The Archaeological Survey of India has protected the Imambara since 1920, and Rumi Darwaza stands just outside it.

items.body: Go early and give yourself time to get lost in the Bhul Bhulaiya.

The Husainabad Imambara, better known as the Chota Imambara, was commissioned by Muhammad Ali Shah, the third King of Oudh (1837–1842), and holds his tomb and his mother's. Its palace-like tomb is crowned by a golden dome and spire.

Inside, the rooms glitter with gilding, mirrors and Belgian crystal chandeliers, which are lit during Muharram and other religious occasions. The 221-foot Husainabad Clock Tower stands nearby.

overview.text:
Rumi Darwaza stands just outside the north-west corner of the Bara Imambara. Built in 1784, it is a monumental gateway whose arch rises to nearly sixty feet, covered in carving and crowned with a turret.

Local tradition says it copies the Sublime Porte in Istanbul — hence its name, the Turkish Gate. Like the Imambara, it was begun during a famine to give people work. Traffic still passes through it, so the best views are from the Imambara side.

overview.text:
The Residency was built during the reigns of Nawab Asaf-ud-Daulah and Nawab Saadat Ali Khan II, between 1780 and 1800, as the home of the British Resident. It suffered heavy damage during the 1857 uprising, when it was besieged, and its battered buildings have since been restored.

Today the ruins stand among lawns and flowerbeds, with a cemetery holding hundreds of graves from the siege. The Archaeological Survey of India runs the 1857 Memorial Museum inside the complex.

overview.text:
The Husainabad Clock Tower rises 221 feet near the Chota Imambara. It was designed by Richard Roskell Bayne and was once believed to be the largest clock tower in the Indian subcontinent.

It was paid for from the Husainabad endowment left by Muhammad Ali Shah, who also built the Chota Imambara. The open square around it is a good place to pause between the Imambaras.

images.alt: Plates of galouti kebabs and parathas on a red tabletop at Tunday Kababi in Lucknow
images.caption: Tunday kebabs

overview.text:
Some of Lucknow's best food is on the street, in the old markets of Chowk and Aminabad. The original Tunday Kababi, home of the legendary galouti kebab, is in Chowk and serves only beef; the Aminabad outlet serves mutton too. The shop is named after its one-armed founding cook.

Start the day the Lucknow way with nalli nihari and kulchas, or a vegetarian Rastogi breakfast of khasta kachori and aloo-chana. In the evening, wander Aminabad for kebabs, chaat and kulfi, and finish with paan. In winter, look out for malai makhan, a sweet milk foam with pistachios.

places.name: Kushinagar
places.summary: Where the Buddha attained mahaparinirvana: the reclining Buddha temple, Ramabhar Stupa, a museum and temples from across Asia.
places.seoTitle: Kushinagar Travel Guide: Buddhist Sites & How to Reach
places.seoDescription: Visit Kushinagar, where the Buddha passed into mahaparinirvana: the reclining Buddha temple, Ramabhar Stupa, the museum and getting there from Gorakhpur.

images.alt: The brick dome of Ramabhar Stupa among palm trees and lawns in Kushinagar
images.caption: Ramabhar Stupa, Kushinagar

overview.text:
Kushinagar is where Gautama Buddha attained mahaparinirvana, his final passing, which makes it one of the most important pilgrimage places in Buddhism. Pilgrims have come since ancient times — the Chinese travellers Faxian and Xuanzang both wrote about it.

The Mahaparinirvana Temple, among the ruins of 5th-century monasteries, holds a 6.1-metre reclining Buddha found in 1876, and the 15-metre Ramabhar Stupa marks the site linked to the cremation. A museum displays excavated finds, and temples built by Chinese, Japanese and Thai Buddhists show how far Kushinagar's pull reaches.

how_to_reach.text: Gorakhpur is the usual gateway: its railway station is about 51 km away, with direct trains from Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Lucknow and other cities, and you can fly into Gorakhpur and drive on. Kushinagar lies on NH 28, with UPSRTC buses.

items.body: Dress modestly and walk clockwise around stupas.
Combine Kushinagar with Sarnath, near Varanasi, where the Buddha gave his first sermon.

places.seoDescription: The Mahaparinirvana Temple in Kushinagar: the 6.1-metre reclining Buddha found by Carlleyle in 1876, the monastery ruins and how to visit respectfully.

images.alt: Devotees around the gilded reclining Buddha draped in yellow cloth inside the Mahaparinirvana Temple, Kushinagar
images.caption: The reclining Buddha

overview.text:
The Mahaparinirvana Temple holds the great reclining Buddha of Kushinagar: a statue 6.1 metres (20 feet) long, uncovered by the archaeologist Archibald Carlleyle in 1876 when he exposed the Mahaparinirvana stupa. The Buddha lies on his right side, in the moment of his final passing.

The temple stands among the ruins of monasteries founded in the 5th century AD. Pilgrims from across Asia drape the statue in cloth and sit in meditation — visit quietly and take your shoes off before entering.

items.body: Visit early in the morning for a quieter moment with the statue.
Ramabhar Stupa is a short ride away.

Ramabhar Stupa rises 15 metres in green, quiet grounds on the edge of Kushinagar. It is the most important pilgrim spot for Buddhists here, associated with the Buddha's final rites after his mahaparinirvana.

Walk around it clockwise as pilgrims do, and pair it with the Mahaparinirvana Temple and its reclining Buddha.

places.name: Akbar's Tomb, Sikandra
places.summary: Emperor Akbar's mausoleum, finished by Jahangir in 1613, in a 119-acre garden on the Agra–Mathura road where blackbuck graze.
places.seoTitle: Akbar's Tomb Sikandra: Timings, Tickets & History
places.seoDescription: Visit Akbar's Tomb at Sikandra, Agra: finished by Jahangir in 1613, its five-storey design and great gateway, blackbuck in the garden, hours and online tickets.

images.alt: The red sandstone gateway of Akbar's Tomb with white marble minarets at Sikandra, Agra
images.caption: Gateway of Akbar's Tomb

overview.text:
Emperor Akbar's mausoleum was begun by Akbar himself and completed by his son Jahangir in 1613. It stands in a vast 119-acre charbagh garden at Sikandra, on the Agra–Mathura road, and its five-storeyed sandstone-and-marble design and grand gateway blend Hindu, Islamic and Persian motifs.

Herds of blackbuck graze in the gardens. The tomb of Mariam-uz-Zamani, Akbar's wife, is 1 km away, and Sikandra is an easy stop on the drive between Agra and Mathura.

items.body: Sunrise to sunset, every day.

guides.seoDescription: Visiting the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya: free darshan and aarti passes, Mangal, Shringar and Shayan aarti times, helpdesk, getting there and tips.

body.intro: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir is now one of India's most visited temples. Here's how to plan a calm, well-organised visit.

sections.heading: Passes are free
sections.text: The Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra trust issues passes for darshan and aarti, and charges no fee for them. Reserve yours on the trust's website before you travel and carry the ID you booked with.

sections.heading: The temple
sections.text: The temple is built entirely of stone in the Nagara style and rises 161 feet including its spire. The 51-inch Ram Lalla idol stands in the sanctum.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.text: Maharishi Valmiki International Airport is about 10 km from Ayodhya Dham; Ayodhya Dham and Ayodhya Cantt are the railway stations; and the city is about 130 km from Lucknow by road.

sections.heading: Help

guides.seoTitle: Best Time to Visit Uttar Pradesh: Weather & Festivals
guides.seoDescription: When to visit Uttar Pradesh: cool winters, hot loo summers, the monsoon, and festival dates for the Magh Mela, Lathmar Holi, Janmashtami and Dev Deepavali.

body.intro: Uttar Pradesh is a plains state with big seasonal swings. Choose your months by the weather — or by the festival you want to see.

sections.heading: Winter: the easy season
sections.text: In Lucknow, winters are cool and dry from late November to February, and October to March is the pleasant season in Mathura. In Varanasi, autumn is the best time of all.

sections.heading: Summer and monsoon
sections.text: From late March to early June it is hot; dry winds called loo blow across the state in summer. After that the south-west monsoon brings most of the year's rain.

guides.summary: The airports, railway stations and roads for Lucknow, Varanasi, Ayodhya, Prayagraj, Mathura and Kushinagar — and the distances between them.
guides.seoTitle: How to Reach Uttar Pradesh: Airports, Trains & Roads
guides.seoDescription: Getting to and around Uttar Pradesh: Lucknow, Varanasi, Ayodhya, Prayagraj and Agra airports, main stations, expressways, UPSRTC buses and city distances.

body.intro: Uttar Pradesh is large, and its great sights are spread across the state. Use the closest airport for each city and the train or road between them.

items.title: Lucknow
items.body: Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport, 14 km from the city, with flights across India and abroad.

items.title: Varanasi
items.body: LBS airport at Babatpur, 22 km from the city and 30 km from Sarnath.

items.title: Ayodhya
items.body: Maharishi Valmiki International Airport, about 10 km from Ayodhya Dham.

items.title: Prayagraj

items.title: Agra

sections.heading: Trains
sections.text: Lucknow's Charbagh is the state's busiest junction; Ayodhya Dham, Prayagraj Junction and Mathura Junction are the main stations for those cities, and Gorakhpur (51 km away) is the railhead for Kushinagar.

sections.heading: Roads and buses
sections.text: The Agra and Purvanchal expressways link Lucknow with Agra and eastern UP, and the Noida–Agra expressway runs past Mathura. UPSRTC buses run round the clock; Lucknow's Alambagh terminal connects to the Metro.

sections.heading: Distances to know
sections.text: Ayodhya is about 130 km from Lucknow, 160 km from Prayagraj and 200 km from Varanasi by road. Mathura is 145 km from Delhi and 58 km from Agra.

guides.seoDescription: What to eat in Lucknow: galouti kebabs at Tunday Kababi, Awadhi biryani, nalli nihari, khasta kachori, malai makhan, and the Chowk and Aminabad food lanes.

body.intro: Lucknow's food is a legacy of the Nawabs of Awadh. This is what to eat, and where.

sections.heading: The kebab
sections.text: The galouti kebab is Lucknow's signature. The original Tunday Kababi is in Chowk and serves only beef; the Aminabad outlet serves mutton as well. The shop is named after its one-armed founding cook.

sections.heading: Awadhi classics
sections.text: Look for Lucknowi biryani, and the slow-cooked dum dishes of Awadhi cuisine — dum gosht and nihari.

sections.heading: Breakfast
sections.text: Locals breakfast on nalli nihari with kulchas; vegetarians can try a Rastogi breakfast of khasta kachori and aloo-chana.

sections.heading: Where to eat

sections.heading: Winter treat

guides.summary: Braj celebrates Holi like nowhere else. When and where Lathmar Holi happens, what to expect, and how to plan your stay.
guides.seoTitle: Lathmar Holi Guide: Barsana, Nandgaon, Mathura & Vrindavan
guides.seoDescription: Plan Holi in Braj: Lathmar Holi in Barsana and Nandgaon, Holi in Mathura and Vrindavan, Rasiya songs, where to stay and tips for visitors.

body.intro: Holi is celebrated across India, but in Braj — Krishna's land around Mathura — it lasts for days and has traditions found nowhere else.

sections.heading: Lathmar Holi
sections.text: In February or March, Barsana celebrates Lathmar Holi over two days: Nandgaon's men come to Barsana's Radha Rani Temple, and the next day Barsana's women go to Nandgaon. The women playfully beat the men with bamboo sticks as Holi songs are sung.

sections.heading: Holi in Mathura
sections.text: Holi in March is one of the most festive times to be in Mathura, along with Janmashtami.

sections.heading: Songs of Braj
sections.text: Rasiya songs — love songs of Radha and Krishna — are always sung at Holi in Braj.

sections.heading: Plan ahead
sections.text: Barsana is about 40 km from Mathura, and the towns fill up fast. Book early, and remember Mathura and Vrindavan are vegetarian and alcohol-free.

checklist: Book your room months ahead
Wear old clothes
Protect your phone and camera

guides.title: Prayagraj guide: the Triveni Sangam, Magh Mela and Kumbh
guides.summary: How to visit the Sangam by boat, when the Magh Mela and Kumbh happen, and what else to see in Prayagraj.
guides.seoDescription: Visit the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj: boats from the fort ghat, hours, Magh Mela dates, the Kumbh, the reclining Hanuman temple and nearby sights.

body.intro: Prayagraj's Triveni Sangam is one of the holiest places in Hinduism. Here's how to visit — on a quiet morning or at a great mela.

sections.heading: The Sangam
sections.text: The brown Ganga meets the green Yamuna about 7 km from Civil Lines, below the ramparts of Akbar's fort. Hire a boat at the ghat near the fort; priests on mid-river platforms help pilgrims with the ritual bath. Incredible India lists the Sangam as open 5 am to 7 pm.

sections.heading: Magh Mela
sections.text: Every year from mid-January to mid-February, starting on Makar Sankranti, a tented township rises at the Sangam for the Magh Mela, with important bathing dates over 45 days.

sections.heading: Kumbh
sections.text: The Kumbh is held at the Sangam once every twelve years — India's largest religious gathering.

sections.heading: Nearby
sections.text: In Daraganj, the Lete Hue Hanuman temple has a 20-foot reclining Hanuman. In the city, visit Anand Bhawan, Khusro Bagh and the Allahabad Museum.

body.intro: Uttar Pradesh holds two of the most sacred places in Buddhism — the site of the Buddha's first sermon and the site of his final passing.

sections.heading: Sarnath
sections.text: Near Varanasi, Sarnath is where the Buddha gave his first sermon to his five companions. See the 42-metre Dhamekh Stupa and the Chaukhandi Stupa.

sections.heading: Kushinagar
sections.text: Kushinagar is where the Buddha attained mahaparinirvana. The Mahaparinirvana Temple holds a 6.1-metre reclining Buddha found in 1876, and the 15-metre Ramabhar Stupa is the town's most important pilgrim spot. Chinese, Japanese and Thai temples stand nearby.

sections.heading: Getting between them
sections.text: Kushinagar is reached via Gorakhpur, whose railway station is about 51 km away; Sarnath is reached from Varanasi.

sections.heading: More Buddhist places
sections.text: Kapilvastu and Sravasti are also in Uttar Pradesh.

Walk clockwise around stupas
Plan Gorakhpur as your Kushinagar gateway
